mechanism.goal: Explain a causal or proposed biological sequence without implying more certainty than the reviewed evidence supports.
composition: Use a single left-to-right or top-to-bottom pathway with 3–5 stages.
Give each stage one focal biological structure and one concise label.
Use arrows only for relationships stated in the evidence payload.
Visually separate directly observed steps from inferred or model-supported steps.
qa: Every arrow direction matches the written synthesis.
No structure resembles a different molecule, organ, cell, or organism.
No proposed mechanism is styled as established fact.

comparison.goal: Compare outcomes, populations, interventions, or explanations without allowing layout area to imply an unsupported effect size.
composition: Use aligned columns or rows with the same visual weight unless magnitude is explicitly encoded.
Keep comparison dimensions identical and in the same order.
Place the most decision-relevant difference first.
State incompatible denominators or populations directly in the panel.
qa: Equal-area elements do not imply unequal magnitude.
Unequal-area elements are proportional to verified values.
Cross-panel comparisons are either valid or explicitly prohibited.

quantitative.goal: Show verified numerical estimates, uncertainty, scales, and denominators with geometry that is mathematically faithful.
composition: Use a standard plot form appropriate to the values: dot-and-whisker, line, bar, or scatter.
Label axes and units and include tick marks; do not use background gridlines.
Use direct labels or a compact key with black text and coloured swatches.
Keep incompatible scales or denominators in clearly separated panels.
qa: Every plotted coordinate is proportional to the supplied data.
Every confidence or credible interval has the supplied endpoints.
No axis, tick, value, unit, sample size, or denominator is invented or altered.
If image generation cannot satisfy exact geometry after one targeted correction, use an evidence-card comparison or the deterministic renderer fallback.

evidence-map.goal: Show how evidence types, populations, outcomes, and limitations relate without pretending that study count alone equals evidence strength.
composition: Group studies or findings by the review's actual decision dimensions.
Use position and concise labels before colour.
Reserve a small explicit legend for evidence-strength or uncertainty encoding.
Keep review-level synthesis visually distinct from individual studies.
qa: Node size, colour, and position have defined meanings.
Study quantity is not presented as quality unless the review supports that inference.
Contradictory and null findings remain visible.

timeline.goal: Show an evidence-backed sequence through time, distinguishing event time, measurement time, and publication time.
composition: Use one dominant chronological axis with evenly interpretable spacing.
Label the time basis and units explicitly.
Use lanes only for genuinely different processes or evidence classes.
Keep callouts concise and place them on alternating sides when useful.
qa: Temporal spacing is proportional unless explicitly labelled schematic.
No event appears earlier or later than the verified record.
Different time bases are not silently mixed.

mindmap.goal: Expose the explanatory structure of the review as a readable hierarchy rather than a decorative radial graphic.
composition: Put the sharpened question at the root and use 4–7 primary branches.
Use short labels and no more than two branch depths unless the topic requires it.
Use a consistent evidence-strength encoding and a compact legend.
Minimize crossing connectors and preserve generous node spacing.
qa: Every branch maps to a reviewed section or finding.
Branch size does not imply effect size unless explicitly defined.
Limitations and contrary evidence are not visually subordinated.
